original_value: Blockchain technology enables a decentralized and distributed environment with no need for a central authority. Transactions are simultaneously secure and trustworthy due to the use of cryptographic principles. In recent years, blockchain technology has become very trendy and penetrated different domains, mostly due to the popularity of cryptocurrencies. One field where blockchain technology has tremendous potential is healthcare, due to the need for a more patient-centric approach to healthcare systems and to connect disparate systems and increase the accuracy of electronic healthcare records (EHRs). In this systematic review, an analysis of state-of-the-art blockchain research in the field of healthcare is conducted. The aim is to reveal the potential applications of the technology and to highlight the challenges and possible directions of blockchain research in healthcare. First, background information is discussed, followed by a description of the exact methodology used in this paper. Next, an analysis of the results is given, which includes a bibliometric overview, an analysis of gathered data and its properties, and the results of a literature quality assessment. Lastly, there is a discussion of the results from the analysis. The findings indicate that blockchain technology research in healthcare is increasing and it is mostly used for data sharing, managing health records and access control. Other scenarios are very rare. Most research is aimed at presenting novel structural designs in the form of frameworks, architectures or models. Findings also show that technical details about the used blockchain elements are not given in most of the analyzed publications and that most research does not present any prototype implementation or implementation details. Often even with a prototype implementation, no details about blockchain elements are given.

result.paraphrase: Blockchain technology creates a decentralized, distributed setting without requiring a central authority. By using cryptographic principles, transactions are both secure and trustworthy. In recent years, it has become highly popular and has spread across many domains, largely because of the rise of cryptocurrencies. Healthcare is one area where blockchain holds significant promise, as there is a need for more patient-centered healthcare systems and for linking disparate systems while improving the accuracy of electronic healthcare records (EHRs). This systematic review analyzes state-of-the-art blockchain research in healthcare. Its purpose is to identify potential applications of the technology and to point out the challenges and possible future directions of blockchain research in healthcare. The paper first presents background information and then explains the exact methodology used. It then discusses the results, including a bibliometric overview, analysis of the collected data and its properties, and the outcome of a literature quality assessment. Finally, the results are discussed. The findings show that blockchain research in healthcare is growing and is used mainly for data sharing, health record management, and access control. Other use cases are rare. Most studies focus on proposing new structural designs in the form of frameworks, architectures, or models. The findings also indicate that technical details about the blockchain elements used are absent in most of the analyzed publications, and that most research does not include a prototype implementation or implementation details. Even when a prototype is presented, details about the blockchain elements are often still missing.
